The claim text is at docs/external/configuration.md:161. The validator _normalize_standing_instructions (src/sqllens/config.py:487-510) is a pydantic field_validator on AgentRuntimeConfig.standing_instructions. It checks every line from text.splitlines() against STANDING_INSTRUCTIONS_DELIMITERS using line.strip() (503-504), so an indented fence line or one with trailing whitespace is caught. It raises ValueError, so the config is rejected at load. splitlines also splits on \r and other Unicode line separators. A fence that differs in case or dash count does not equal the fence constants (434-435). It is not the fence line, so accepting it matches the claim. A fence that is not on a line of its own is also accepted, which matches the 'on a line of its own' wording at config.py:433. I found no input that breaks the claim.

config.py:489-510 _normalize_standing_instructions: value.strip() (line 494); empty or whitespace-only returns None (495-496); len(text) > MAX_STANDING_INSTRUCTIONS_CHARS (=10_000, line 430) raises ValueError (497-502), which pydantic turns into a ValidationError at config load. Traced inputs: exactly 10,000 chars after strip is accepted; 10,001 is rejected; whitespace-only becomes None. Whitespace padding beyond the limit does not count since the length check is on the stripped text. None means no section is added: default.py:71 also strips to None, 137-138 returns base_prompt verbatim, and 170 and 361 add sections only when the value is not None. So the prompt is the same as with the setting unset.

Absolute-claim input: base_prompt path, which has no such rules to refer to, so it does not break the claim about the default prompt.

config.py:487-510 `_normalize_standing_instructions` returns None for None or blank text and raises ValueError when the stripped text is over 10,000 characters (MAX_STANDING_INSTRUCTIONS_CHARS, line 430). An instruction to ask keeps the choice open, and a memory note or saved pair does not settle it. config.py:503-509 rejects any splitlines() line whose str.strip() equals either fence. str.strip removes all Unicode whitespace (NBSP, U+2003, etc.), so a fence padded by non-ASCII whitespace is rejected. Interior-spacing variants are not the fence line the builder emits (default.py:113,115 emit the exact constants), so they are not covered by the claim. Bypass trace: a value that skips config validation (direct DefaultSystemPromptBuilder construction) hits the same check at default.py:71-78, which raises ValueError using the same strip/splitlines predicate. So the comment at config.py:432-433 holds on both paths. Attribute mutation after construction is not a shipped caller path.

config.py:691-697 Config(BaseSettings) sets extra="forbid" at top level only. Nested AgentRuntimeConfig is a plain BaseModel (line 439); pydantic default extra is "ignore" and parent model_config is not inherited by nested field models, as the repo's own comments at 241-245 and 413-419 also state. Without line 449 extra="forbid", a misspelt key such as standing_instruction (real field standing_instructions, line ~475) from TOML or SQLLENS_AGENT__ env nested delimiter would be dropped silently. Traced the env path: nested dict goes into AgentRuntimeConfig validation, which ignores extras by default. Claim holds.
